tei:respStmt.tei:name: Efraim Feinstein

tei:editionStmt.tei:edition: Read directly from the scanned 1949 printing, page by page

tei:body.tei:p: Our God and God of our fathers, sustain this child for his father and mother. Let him be called in Israel . . . son of . . . May both husband and wife rejoice in their offspring, as it is written: “Let your parents be happy; let your mother thrill with joy.”

tei:p.tei:seg: “I passed by you and saw you weltering in your blood. Live through your blood—I said to you—live through your blood.”
“He remembers his covenant forever, the word which he pledged for a thousand generations,
the covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
He confirmed the same to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant.”
“Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.”

tei:body.tei:p: “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; his mercy endures forever.” May this child, named . . ., become great. Even as he has been introduced into the covenant, so may he be introduced to the Torah, to the marriage canopy, and to a life of good deeds.
